# Sirach Chapter 3 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 3 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/SIR_003_page_001.jpg

---

**3:1** Listen to me, your father, O children; and act accordingly, so that you may be kept safe.

**3:2** For the Lord honored the father above the children, and confirmed the right of the mother over her sons.

**3:3** Whoever honors his father atones for sins,

**3:4** and whoever glorifies his mother is like one who lays up treasure.

**3:5** Whoever honors his father will be gladdened by his own children, and when he prays he will be heard.

**3:6** Whoever glorifies his father will have long life, and whoever obeys the Lord will give rest to his mother.

**3:7** He who fears the Lord honors his father, and he serves his parents as his masters.

**3:8** Honor your father by word and deed, that a blessing from him may come upon you.

**3:9** For a father's blessing strengthens the houses of the children, but a mother's curse uproots the foundations.

**3:10** Do not glorify yourself by dishonoring your father, for your father's dishonor is no glory to you.

**3:11** For a man's glory comes from the honor of his father, and it is a disgrace for children if their mother is put to shame.

**3:12** My child, help your father in his old age, and do not grieve him as long as he lives.

**3:13** Even if his mind fails, be patient with him; and do not despise him all the days of his life.

**3:14** For kindness to a father will not be forgotten, and it will stand as an atonement for your sins.

**3:15** In the day of your affliction it will be remembered in your favor; like frost in fair weather, your sins will melt away.

**3:16** Whoever abandons his father is like a blasphemer, and whoever angers his mother is cursed by the Lord.

**3:17** My child, perform your tasks with humility; then you will be loved more than a giver of gifts.

**3:18** The greater you are, the more you must humble yourself, and you will find favor before the Lord.

**3:19** Many are lofty and renowned, but to the humble he reveals his mysteries.

**3:20** For the power of the Lord is great, and he is glorified by those who are humble.

**3:21** Seek not what is too difficult for you, nor investigate what is beyond your power.

**3:22** Reflect upon what has been assigned to you, for you do not need what is hidden.

**3:23** Do not meddle in things beyond your tasks, for more is shown to you than human beings understand.

**3:24** For many have been led astray by their own conceit, and wrong opinion has warped their thinking.

**3:25** Without eyes there is no light; without knowledge there is no wisdom.

**3:26** A stubborn mind will be hurt at the end, and one who loves danger will perish in it.

**3:27** A stubborn mind will be burdened with troubles, and the sinner adds sin to sin.

**3:28** For the affliction of the proud there is no healing, for an evil plant has taken root in him.

**3:29** The mind of the intelligent will ponder a parable, and an attentive ear is the desire of the wise.

**3:30** Water extinguishes a blazing fire; so almsgiving atones for sin.

**3:31** Whoever requites good turns is thinking of the future, and when he falls he will find a support.

---

*Translator's Note: Hebrew fragments from Cairo Genizah (MS A) are extant for much of this chapter. The Hebrew ha-mekhabed et aviv = "one who honors his father." Greek parallels the Hebrew closely throughout. v.19 is absent from the main Vaticanus text but present in other witnesses; included here.*
